name: strike-from-the-mist-prepare-2-paid-cannot-be-intercepted
notes: Strike from the Mist (DHn9J7gX6g, WATER ASSASSIN ATTACK, reserve 2, printed power 2): "Prepare 2. [Class Bonus] As long as Strike from the Mist was prepared, it can't be intercepted." Player 2's champion is Tristan, Shadowdancer (ASSASSIN, UMBRA) patched in with extra lineage cards to unlock the card's element; ATTACK cards cannot be played by the first player on turn 1, so player 1 ends turn 1 and player 2 plays the card with real actions (10002 FSM play, 100 reserve payments / YES-NO answer / attack target). Player 1 controls a Swift Recruit (Intercept ally, p1Field-1) so interceptability is observable (an interceptor prompt is queued for player 1 exactly when the attack is interceptable). Champion holds 2 preparation counters; player 2 pays Prepare 2 and attacks player 1's champion: no interceptor prompt is queued, Swift Recruit is untouched and the champion takes the 2 damage.

rulesClauses: [Class Bonus] As long as Strike from the Mist was prepared, it can't be intercepted.

engineBug.summary: FIXED. The CardEditor ability row for this card never queued the fixed Prepare cost: no $cardActivatedAbilities['DHn9J7gX6g:0'] entry existed (or, for the Strike from the Mist stub, it was an empty '(engine)' body), so OnCardActivated() queued no 'Pay Prepare N?' decision and wasPrepared was never YES. Live state dump on HEAD 47028d36 before the fix: after the last reserve payment the decision queue went straight to the attack-target / ally-target choice (no YESNO), preparation counters stayed untouched, and answering YES was rejected as 'Invalid selection' (or silently ignored) -- so the card's 'if prepared' rider was unreachable. Fix: $cardActivatedAbilities['DHn9J7gX6g:0'] (previously an empty '(engine)' stub) now queues the Prepare 2 cost (GAQueueFixedPrepare(player, 2)); the 'can't be intercepted' check itself already lives in CombatLogic.php (AttackBypassesInterceptAndTaunt reads the PREPARED intent tag and the ASSASSIN class bonus) but the tag was never set.
